action.action-desc: Mr. Johnson (for himself, Mr. Peters, Mr. Wyden, and Mr. Wicker) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs
Reported by Mr. Johnson, with an amendment

form.official-title: To modernize the REAL ID Act of 2005, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the REAL ID Modernization Act.

subsection.text: Section 201 of the REAL ID Act of 2005 (division B of Public Law 109–13; 49 U.S.C. 30301 note) is amended—

subparagraph.text: by striking The term driver’s license means and inserting the following: “The term ‘driver’s license’—
means
by striking Code. and inserting the following: “Code; and
includes driver’s licenses stored or accessed via electronic means, such as mobile or digital driver’s licenses, which have been issued in accordance with regulations prescribed by the Secretary.
by striking The term identification card means and inserting the following: “The term ‘identification card’—
means
by striking State. and inserting the following: “State; and

includes identification cards stored or accessed via electronic means, such as mobile or digital identification cards, which have been issued in accordance with regulations prescribed by the Secretary.

subsection.text: Section 202 of the REAL ID Act of 2005 (division B of Public Law 109–13; 49 U.S.C. 30301 note) is amended—

subparagraph.text: in paragraph (2), by striking , in consultation with the Secretary of Transportation,; and
by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.text: The presentation of a digital image of a driver’s license or identification card to an official of a Federal agency may not be construed to grant consent for such Federal agency—

subparagraph.text: to examine any data (other than the digital document being presented) contained on the personal electronic device on which the license or card is displayed; or
to otherwise search or seize such device.
in the subsection header, by striking document and inserting driver’s license and identification card;
in the matter preceding paragraph (1), by inserting , or as part of, after features on;

in paragraph (5), by inserting , which may be taken at the time the person applies for a driver’s license or identification card or may be a digital photograph of the person that is already on file with the State if the photograph was taken during the 6-year period preceding such application before the period at the end;
in paragraph (6), by striking principle and inserting principal; and
in paragraph (8)—

clause.text: by striking Physical security and inserting Security; and

subparagraph.text: in paragraph (1)—

clause.text: in subparagraph (C), by striking Proof of the and inserting The; and
in subparagraph (D), by striking Documentation showing the and inserting The;

subparagraph.text: by redesignating paragraph (3) as paragraph (4);
by inserting after paragraph (2) the following:

paragraph.header: Electronic presentation of identity and lawful status information
paragraph.text: A State may accept information required under paragraphs (1) and (2) through the use of electronic transmission methods if—

subparagraph.text: the Secretary issues regulations regarding such electronic transmission that—

clause.text: describe the categories of information eligible for electronic transmission; and

subclause.text: to ensure the authenticity of the information transmitted;
to protect personally identifiable information; and
to detect and prevent identity fraud; and

subparagraph.text: the State certifies to the Department of Homeland Security that its use of such electronic methods complies with regulations issued by the Secretary.
in paragraph (4)(A), as redesignated, by striking each document and inserting the information and documentation; and
in paragraph (7), by striking document materials and papers and inserting materials, records, and data;
in paragraph (8), by striking security clearance requirements and inserting background checks; and
in paragraph (9), by striking fraudulent document recognition and inserting fraud detection and prevention.

subsection.header: Permanent extension of grants to States
subsection.text: Section 204(b) of the REAL ID Act of 2005 (division B of Public Law 109–13; 49 U.S.C. 30301 note) is amended by striking for each of the fiscal years 2005 through 2009.
Section 205(a) of the REAL ID Act of 2005 (division B of Public Law 109–13; 49 U.S.C. 30301 note) is amended to read as follows:
At the Secretary’s discretion, the promulgation of regulations and the administration of this title may be made without regard to—

paragraph.text: chapter 35 of title 44, United States Code (commonly known as the Paperwork Reduction Act); and
the notice and comment and delayed effective date provisions under section 553 of title 5, United States Code.

subsection.header: Notification of REAL ID Act of 2005 requirements
subsection.text: The REAL ID Act of 2005 (division B of Public Law 109–13; 49 U.S.C. 30301 note) is amended by adding at the end the following:

section.text: During the 15-month period beginning 90 days before the date on which Federal agencies will no longer accept, for official purposes, driver’s licenses and identification cards that do not comply with the requirements under section 202, aircraft operators and third party reservation entities shall notify passengers, to the extent practicable, about the requirements and enforcement deadlines under this Act.

Notwithstanding any other provision of law, beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act, a State does not need to require an applicant for a driver’s license or identification card to provide separate documentation of the applicant’s Social Security account number or address of principal residence in order to comply with section 201 of the REAL ID Act of 2005, as amended by section 2(a).
This Act may be cited as the REAL ID Modernization Act.

subsection.header: Notification of REAL ID Act of 2005 requirements
subsection.text: The REAL ID Act of 2005 (division B of Public Law 109–13; 49 U.S.C. 30301 note) is amended by adding at the end the following:
